editorial:
You follow a tiny boy named Saroo who gets separated from his brother and ends up alone in Calcutta. The first half feels raw and scary as he dodges danger and searches for home. Later, he is adopted by a loving Australian couple and grows into a young man who cannot shake the feeling that someone is missing him. The story moves between childhood fear and adult longing, so you feel both the danger of the streets and the ache of memory.

The acting is strong, especially from the child actor and Dev Patel, and the pacing keeps you invested without rushing. The emotional payoff is huge, though some middle scenes feel a bit slow. If you enjoy true stories about family, identity, and hope, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Saroo uses Google Earth and old memories to trace his hometown, then travels to India and finds his mother waiting in the same village. She never stopped hoping. He also learns his brother died years earlier, which makes the reunion bittersweet. The twist is that his real name was Sheru, and the title Lion comes from that name. You leave feeling relieved, sad, and deeply moved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about family, identity, and hope.
